answer: The mechanism is a local sensor challenge registry: each identity embeds a hardware security kernel that signs time-stamped readings from one unique physical site. A site must remain instrumented for weeks; tundra deployments raise the cost because power and enclosure must survive cold. A meadow site must submit weekly spectra, and duplicate or relayed readings fail cross-correlation, so an attacker pays a fresh sensor kit, site access, and calibration per identity.
